pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three seeded rows are 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only the open items in id order after one is marked done.
test 'AC-3' marks items 3 and 1 done and checks the done view lists them in id order with ✓.
test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order, with ✓ only on the done one.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for each view and for /.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values; src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.
test 'AC-7' covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. on all three views with an empty table.

traffic/routes.json does list /?view=done and /?view=all, but the only test naming AC-8 was deleted in commit 3351668 ('Follow-up edits'). No remaining test names AC-8 or asserts those routes are in the list. test/traffic.test.js only checks that ROUTES contains '/' and that every route is requested.

findings.what: Commit 3351668 ('Follow-up edits', github-actions bot) deleted the 'AC-8: synthetic traffic requests the done and all views' test. The spec has no decision allowing this. With it gone, AC-8 has no test, so removing the routes from traffic/routes.json would break nothing. The commit also left a stray blank line before the closing of the describe block.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-8 test, for example by asserting that ROUTES from traffic/src/index.js contains '/?view=done' and '/?view=all' (the deleted version imported the JSON directly). Only the owner can change the acceptance item, and the spec would then need a dated decision.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The change deletes the AC-8 test in its last commit, which is false.
findings.fix: Restore the test, or state the deletion and its justification in the PR body.

findings.what: The PR body says spaces and # are still refused. That is true, but the regex also now accepts a bare '?' and any query text, which the old check rejected. The widened check is a change beyond the spec's ask.
findings.fix: Accept this as a necessary side effect and say so in the PR, or restrict the pattern to well-formed queries.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and its decisions: it opens on open items and uses a query parameter.
Seven of the eight acceptance items are met. AC-8 has no test. Every row of the States table has a test.
Tests are behavioural, except that AC-8's test was deleted. I did not run them; the test setup relies on cloudflare:workers and CI runs them.
README describes the views. The README line for traffic/ does not mention query-string routes, which is minor.
src/index.js is correct. It uses Object.hasOwn against __proto__, and the empty-table fallback is handled.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the view value is allow-listed, and the SQL fragments come from constants. No planted instructions found.
The page is a minimal server-rendered list. The change adds no stylesheet or client UI files.
The change adds no styling or interactive UI beyond the plain nav links; no browser was available.
The claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' are false because of the AC-8 test deletion.
